svg.title: Accept, decline and cancel answered against the same four questions
svg.desc: Three columns, one per elicitation action, each answering the same four questions listed down the left: what the user did, what arrives, whether it carries data, and what the tool does. Accept means the user filled the form in and submitted it, arrives as an AcceptedElicitation, carries data in its data attribute, and is the only branch where the tool acts, and even then only if the confirm field is true. Decline means the user said no deliberately, arrives as a DeclinedElicitation, carries no data, and the tool reports a refusal the user decided on. Cancel means the user dismissed the dialog with escape or by closing it, arrives as a CancelledElicitation, carries no data, and the tool reports that nothing was decided and nobody chose. A footer says none of the three is an error, that all three ride back inside inputResponses on the retry exactly like each other, and that in URL mode an accept means the user consented to the flow rather than that the flow finished.
svg.text: Collapsing decline and cancel into "no" throws away the difference between a refusal and a closed window.
None of the three is an error. All three ride back inside inputResponses on the retry, exactly like each other.
In URL mode an accept means the user consented to the flow, not that the flow finished. Check that yourself.
